title: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Catching up and catching heat
author: Cherlynn Low

findings.subject: apple-watch-series-12
findings.text: The new sensors measure background heart rate every 5 seconds (it was every 5 minutes) and heart rate variability every 5 minutes; readings stayed within two beats per minute of a Fitbit worn for comparison.

findings.subject: apple-watch-series-12
findings.text: Battery life matched the Series 11, with about half the charge left after quieter days; a 12-minute charge took it from 51% to 79%.

findings.subject: apple-watch-series-12
findings.text: New wrist gestures help hands-free use, but the new app grid sometimes put unexpected apps first, and the Readiness score needs a week of baseline data.

findings.subject: apple-watch-series-12
findings.text: Responsive throughout testing, with no stutters or lag.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 review: More personal than ever before
author: Chance Miller

findings.subject: apple-watch-series-12
findings.text: The S11 chip with twice the memory (4 GB) made apps open and menus scroll faster.

findings.subject: apple-watch-series-12
findings.text: The display area is 2% smaller than before, which the reviewer could not notice in use.

findings.subject: apple-watch-series-12
findings.text: Heart rate every 5 seconds, better heart rate variability tracking, a daytime Vitals view and a new Readiness score.

findings.subject: apple-watch-ultra-4
findings.text: Apple rates it at 50 hours of normal use (42 before); the reviewer got about 48 hours on one charge including 90 minutes of workouts.

findings.subject: apple-watch-ultra-4
findings.text: Gets the same new health sensors and Readiness score as the Series 12.

title: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE review: An incremental price hike for incremental updates
author: Mat Smith
method: Experience review with a video playback battery test; score 67 out of 100.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-s26-fe
findings.text: The 6.7-inch 120 Hz OLED is crisp and vivid, though dimmer at its peak than the other S26 models.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-s26-fe
findings.text: Just over 21 hours in Engadget's video playback test, noticeably less than the S26+ with a battery of the same capacity; it needed charging every day.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-s26-fe
findings.text: The Exynos 2500 handled most tasks but struggled with demanding games, and the camera app sometimes felt slow.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-s26-fe
findings.text: The 50 MP main camera does well in good light; the 8 MP telephoto gave blurry or overexposed shots.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-s26-fe
findings.text: Costs US$50 more than the previous FE for small changes, which makes discounted older models hard to ignore.

title: Apple AirPods 5 review: The choice is clear
author: Billy Steele

findings.subject: apple-airpods-5
findings.text: Fuller bass and more instrument detail than before; noise cancelling handled steady background hum well, though voices still got through.

findings.subject: apple-airpods-5
findings.text: About 5 to 7 hours with noise cancelling on the higher model and 4 to 6 on the base model; five minutes of charging gives about an hour.

findings.subject: apple-airpods-5
findings.text: The US$149 model with the wireless charging case and volume gestures was judged the better buy than the US$129 one.

title: Google Pixel 11 Review: The smarter flagship evolves
author: Srivatsan Sridhar
method: Experience review with stress testing (reviewed in India).

findings.subject: google-pixel-11
findings.text: A bright 6.3-inch 120 Hz OLED that is easy to read outdoors, but without an LTPO panel.

findings.subject: google-pixel-11
findings.text: The Tensor G6 felt smooth in daily use but throttled in long gaming sessions; the phone reached 45 °C in a stress test, and it has no vapour chamber.

findings.subject: google-pixel-11
findings.text: Strong daylight and low-light photos from the new 48 MP main camera and the 5x telephoto.

findings.subject: google-pixel-11
findings.text: More than a day of typical use from the 4,985 mAh battery.

findings.subject: google-pixel-11
findings.text: 30 W wired charging reached 50% in about 25 minutes.

title: 小米 18 Pro Max 首发评测：最好的小米手机，也是最好玩的小米手机
author: 肖钦鹏

findings.subject: xiaomi-18-pro-max
findings.text: Heat was spread more evenly than on the 17 Pro Max, no longer gathering under the cameras, and sustained performance was steadier.

findings.subject: xiaomi-18-pro-max
findings.text: Two 200 MP cameras (main and telephoto) cover 17–200 mm; the new Leica colour profile recovers more shadow detail, and black-and-white shots were the strongest point.

findings.subject: xiaomi-18-pro-max
findings.text: The 8,500 mAh battery gave over 9 hours of screen-on time on average per day.

findings.subject: xiaomi-18-pro-max
findings.text: The rear screen now sits flush with the camera lenses and matches the main screen's quality; the main screen has very narrow bezels and a hardware privacy mode.

findings.subject: xiaomi-18-pro-max
findings.text: Called the high point of Xiaomi's design in five years, with a more rounded frame that sits better in the hand.

title: HONOR 600 Display: Impressive hardware, MagicOS needs finesse
author: Tamil G
method: A week of everyday use of the display outdoors and in the dark; no lab instruments (the 8,000-nit figure is HONOR's lab claim).

findings.subject: honor-600
findings.text: Easy to read in direct midday sun even without Sunlight Mode, which raises contrast rather than just brightness.

findings.subject: honor-600
findings.text: Dims to 1 nit, comfortable for reading in a dark room; automatic brightness changed smoothly rather than in steps.

findings.subject: honor-600
findings.text: Some eye-comfort modes, such as Defocus Eyecare, made no difference the reviewer could see.

title: A look at ColorOS 17 based on Android 17 on OnePlus 15
author: Srivatsan Sridhar
method: Hands-on with ColorOS 17, which replaces OxygenOS on OnePlus phones worldwide; the speed figures quoted are OnePlus's own.

findings.subject: oneplus-15
findings.text: ColorOS 17 brings a new translucent, light-reactive design and AI tools that save on-screen content and suggest flights, trains and music.

findings.subject: oneplus-15
findings.text: Frame pacing stayed steady during heavy app switching and fast scrolling through large galleries.

title: One UI 9 on the Galaxy S25 vs S26 series: What's different?
method: Side-by-side look at One UI 9 on both series.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-s25
findings.text: The S25 series gets the same new Galaxy AI tools (My FanCam, Call Brief, custom Now Brief cards) and home-screen changes as the S26 series, plus Horizontal Lock video stabilisation.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-s26
findings.text: Only the S26 series offers 100, 50, 48 and 25 fps in Pro video mode at Full HD and UHD, 25 fps at 8K, and 24 MP in the standard Photo mode; the S25 series needs the separate Expert RAW app for 24 MP.

title: iPhone Duo review: The future is foldable
author: Chance Miller
method: Experience review after a week of use.

findings.subject: apple-iphone-duo
findings.text: At 254 g it weighs 5 g more than the iPhone 18 Pro Max but felt more comfortable to hold and carry thanks to its shorter, wider shape; 11.3 mm thick closed and 5.2 mm open.

findings.subject: apple-iphone-duo
findings.text: The hinge holds the phone at many angles for hands-free video calls and StandBy, though opening it is a two-handed job; the reviewer quickly stopped worrying about it.

findings.subject: apple-iphone-duo
findings.text: The 5.4-inch outer screen worked well for messages, notes, reading and social media rather than feeling like a last resort.

findings.subject: apple-iphone-duo
findings.text: Many websites are awkward on the outer screen: Safari's side controls take space and pop-ups can fill the view.

title: Apple iPhone Duo review: A first-class foldable
author: Sam Rutherford
method: Experience review; score 8.8 out of 10. Battery: Engadget's local video rundown.

records.subject: apple-iphone-duo
records.note: 28 h 48 min; the screen used is not stated

findings.subject: apple-iphone-duo
findings.text: Lasted 28 h 48 min in Engadget's video rundown, about half an hour longer than the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (28:14) but short of the Moto Razr Fold (31:00).

findings.subject: apple-iphone-duo
findings.text: 254 g, more than 25% heavier than the Galaxy Z Fold 8; one of the smoothest hinges the reviewer has used.

findings.subject: apple-iphone-duo
findings.text: The matte inner screen cuts reflections and hides the crease well, though a small dip down the middle can be seen when looked for.

findings.subject: apple-iphone-duo
findings.text: Apple's own apps use the big screen well, but many others (Telegram, Gmail) are not yet adapted and leave empty space at the sides.

title: Expectations vs reality: What does the Galaxy Z Fold 8's foldable screen actually feel like?
author: Mihai Matei
method: Three months of everyday use as the writer's only phone.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-z-fold8
findings.text: The inner screen feels and sounds almost like glass to the touch; the crease is slightly visible and can be felt but did not bother the writer.

findings.subject: samsung-galaxy-z-fold8
findings.text: Tapping it with a fingernail is harmless, but dragging a nail across it leaves a permanent mark, and the surface picks up micro-scratches more easily than glass; no marks appeared in three months of normal use.

title: Here's the difference the variable aperture of the iPhone 18 Pro makes at night
author: Ben Lovejoy
method: Night-mode photos in London at f/1.48, f/1.8 and f/4.

findings.subject: apple-iphone-18-pro
findings.text: Opening up from f/1.8 to f/1.48 shortened a Night mode shot only slightly (2.1 s to 1.7 s); closing down to f/4 allowed 4-second exposures that smoothed water and gave lights a starburst.
